about: The last episode of the Fourth Branch. While Lleu Llaw Gyffes is away visiting Math at Caer Dathyl, a hunting party passes his court at Mur Castell, and Blodeuedd, the wife Math and Gwydion made for him out of flowers, invites its lord in for the night: Gronw Pebyr of Penllyn. The two fall in love at a look, and plot Lleu's death. Blodeuedd, feigning a wife's anxiety, draws from Lleu the narrow conditions under which alone he can be killed; Gronw spends a year making the spear, and when Lleu is persuaded to show how he would stand with one foot on a tub and one on a goat, Gronw strikes him from the hill. Lleu flies off as an eagle. Gwydion tracks him by following a sow to an oak where the eagle sits rotting, sings him down with three englynion, and restores him with his staff. Healed, Lleu takes his revenge: Blodeuedd, fleeing, sees her maidens drown and is turned into an owl; Gronw, deserted by his men, must stand where Lleu stood and take Lleu's cast, and the spear goes through the stone he holds up and through him. Lleu takes back his land, and as the story tells is afterwards lord over Gwynedd; and the branch ends.

sentences.t: Ac yna treigylgueith kyrchu a wnaeth parth a Chaer Dathyl e ymwelet a Math uab Mathonwy.
sentences.l: And then one-time making-for he-did towards Caer Dathyl to visit Math son of Mathonwy.
sentences.i: And then, once, he set out for Caer Dathyl to visit Math son of Mathonwy.
sentences.n: This part begins in col. 101 l. 17, in mid-line, straight after the last words of the previous part (… ac y arglwydiaeth); the White Book gives it no large initial. The 'he' is Lleu, now lord in Ardudwy and living at Mur Castell with Blodeuedd. treigylgueith is treigylgweith 'one time, once' (gu for gw). kyrchu a wnaeth 'making for he did' is the narrative pattern of a verbal noun closed by a wnaeth, the preterite of gwneuthur 'do': it means simply 'he made for'. parth a 'towards' (lit. 'side with'); a 'with' causes spirant mutation, Caer > Chaer. e ymwelet a 'to visit': e is y 'to'. uab is mab 'son', soft-mutated after a personal name, as always in 'X son of Y'.

sentences.t: Y dyd yd aeth ef parth a Chaer Tathyl, troi o uywn y llys a wnaet hi.
sentences.l: The day that went he towards Caer Dathyl, turning about within the court she-did.
sentences.i: On the day he went to Caer Dathyl, she was moving about within the court.
sentences.n: Y dyd yd aeth ef 'the day he went': a time phrase with yd, the particle used before a vowel, and no word for 'on'. The scribe writes Caer Tathyl here and Caer Dathyl above; the English keeps Caer Dathyl. troi o uywn y llys a wnaet hi 'turning within the court she did': o uywn is o fewn 'within' (mywn soft-mutated after o). a wnaet: Evans prints a6naet with no h, and the image is clear; the Red Book has a wnaeth hi. The word is kept as the White Book writes it and read as wnaeth, the h of -th lost before hi.

sentences.t: A hi a glywei lef corn, ac yn ol llef y corn llyma hyd blin yn mynet heibaw, a chwn a chynydyon yn y ol.
sentences.l: And she it-was-that heard the cry of-a-horn, and after the cry of the horn, behold a-weary stag going past, and hounds and huntsmen after it.
sentences.i: And she heard the call of a horn, and after the call of the horn there went by a spent stag, with hounds and huntsmen behind it.
sentences.n: A hi a glywei 'and she heard': the subject first, then the particle a, then the verb. This is the 'abnormal sentence', the ordinary order of Middle Welsh narrative prose; nothing is being stressed. glywei is the imperfect of clywet 'hear', soft-mutated after a. lef is llef 'cry', soft-mutated as the object. llyma 'behold, here is' (modern dyma) makes the scene vivid. hyd blin 'a weary stag' (hydd); heibaw 'past' (heibio). a chwn a chynydyon: spirant mutation after a 'and' (cwn 'hounds', kynydyon 'huntsmen', plural of kynyd). yn y ol 'in its track', i.e. after it.

sentences.t: Ac yn ol y cwn a'r kynydyon, bagat o wyr ar traet yn dyuot.
sentences.l: And after the hounds and the huntsmen, a-troop of men on foot coming.
sentences.i: And after the hounds and the huntsmen came a band of men on foot.
sentences.n: A sentence with no finite verb: yn dyuot 'coming' does the work. bagat 'cluster, band' (bagad). o wyr: gwyr 'men' soft-mutated after o. ar traet 'on foot' is written without the soft mutation that ar usually causes (ar draet).

sentences.t: “Ellynghwch was,” heb hi, “e wybot pwy yr yniuer.”
sentences.l: “Let-go a-lad,” said she, “to know who the company.”
sentences.i: “Send a lad,” she said, “to find out who the company are.”
sentences.n: Ellynghwch is the 2nd plural imperative of gellwng 'let go, send', in the form without g that the tale regularly uses (ellwng); she is speaking to her people. was is gwas 'lad, servant', soft-mutated as the object. e wybot is y 'to' + gwybot 'know', soft-mutated. pwy yr yniuer 'who the company': the verb 'is' is left out, as often in a question. yniuer 'host, company' (niver).

sentences.t: Y guas a aeth, a gouyn pwy oedynt.
sentences.l: The lad it-was-that went, and asking who they-were.
sentences.i: The lad went and asked who they were.
sentences.n: Y guas a aeth: the abnormal sentence again (guas = gwas). a gouyn 'and asking': a verbal noun carries the second action on without a new finite verb. oedynt is the 3rd plural imperfect of bot 'be'.

sentences.t: “Gronw Pebyr yw hwnn, y gwr yssyd arglwyd ar Benllyn,” heb wy.
sentences.l: “Gronw Pebyr is this, the man who-is lord over Penllyn,” said they.
sentences.i: “This is Gronw Pebyr, the man who is lord of Penllyn,” they said.
sentences.n: yw 'is' stands after the predicate it identifies: 'Gronw Pebyr is this'. Pebyr 'radiant, bright, strong' (modern pefr) is his epithet. yssyd 'who is' is the relative form of bot. ar Benllyn: Penllyn soft-mutated after ar. Penllyn is the cantref round Llyn Tegid, east of Ardudwy. heb wy 'said they' (wy 'they').

sentences.t: Hynny a dywot y guas idi hitheu.
sentences.l: That it-was-that the lad told to-her for-her-part.
sentences.i: That is what the lad told her.
sentences.n: Hynny a dywot y guas: the object stands first, then a and the verb, then the subject. dywot is the 3rd singular preterite of dywedut 'say, tell'. idi 'to her' is the preposition i conjugated for 3rd singular feminine; hitheu is the conjunctive pronoun 'she in her turn'.

sentences.t: Ynteu a gerdwys yn ol yr hyd.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part it-was-that went after the stag.
sentences.i: Gronw, for his part, went on after the stag.
sentences.n: Ynteu 'he for his part' is Gronw, the conjunctive pronoun marking the change of subject. gerdwys is kerdwys, 3rd singular preterite of kerdet 'walk, go', soft-mutated after a; -wys is the old preterite ending (modern -odd).

sentences.t: Ac ar Auon Gynnwael gordiwes yr hyd a'y lad.
sentences.l: And on the River Cynfael overtaking the stag and killing it.
sentences.i: And on the river Cynfael he overtook the stag and killed it.
sentences.n: Two verbal nouns and no finite verb: gordiwes 'overtake' (goddiweddyd) and llad 'kill'. a'y lad is a 'and' + y 'its' + llad soft-mutated after the masculine possessive: 'and its killing'. Auon Gynnwael is the river Cynfael, the name soft-mutated after the feminine auon. The scribe spells it Gynnwael here, Kynuael and Gynuael later; the English keeps Cynfael throughout. The text itself places the river in Ardudwy (col. 111).

sentences.t: Ac wrth ulingyaw yr hyd, a llithyaw y gwn, ef a uu yny wascawd y nos arnaw.
sentences.l: And while flaying the stag, and feeding the hounds, it it-was-that was until pressed the night on-him.
sentences.i: And what with flaying the stag and giving the hounds their portion, he was kept until night closed in on him.
sentences.n: wrth ulingyaw 'in flaying': blingyaw 'flay' soft-mutated after wrth. llithyaw 'feed the hounds their portion of the kill' (llithio, from llith 'bait'). y gwn 'the hounds': cwn soft-mutated after y, here 'his'. ef a uu yny … 'it was until …': ef is an empty subject, uu is bu 'was', soft after a. yny 'until' takes soft mutation: wascawd is gwascawd, 3rd singular preterite of gwascu 'press', with the old ending -awd. arnaw 'on him' (ar, 3rd singular masculine).

sentences.t: A phan ytoed y dyd yn atueilaw, a'r nos yn nessau, ef a doeth heb porth y llys.
sentences.l: And when was the day declining, and the night drawing-near, he it-was-that came past the gate of the court.
sentences.i: And when the day was failing and night drawing on, he came past the gate of the court.
sentences.n: A phan: pan 'when' with spirant mutation after a. ytoed is yd oed 'was'. atueilaw 'decay, wane' (adfeilio); nessau 'draw near'. heb here is the preposition 'past, beyond' (the same word as 'without'); porth 'gate' is left unmutated after it. doeth is the 3rd singular preterite of dyuot 'come'.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb hi, “ni a gawn yn goganu gan yr unben o'e ady y prytwn y wlat arall, onys guahodwn.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said she, “we it-is-that will-get our reviling by the chieftain for his leaving at this-time to the other land, unless him we-invite.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” she said, “the chieftain will speak ill of us for letting him go off at this hour to another country, if we do not invite him in.”
sentences.n: ni a gawn 'we shall get': cawn is the 1st plural present of cael, which serves as a future, soft-mutated after a. yn goganu 'our reviling': yn is the old spelling of ein 'our', and goganu is 'satirise, speak ill of'. unben 'chieftain'. o'e ady: o 'for' + 'e 'his' + ady. Evans prints ady (checked at zoom 12); the second witness and the Red Book have adu, and the word is read as adu 'leaving, letting go' (gadu, its g lost by soft mutation after the masculine 'e): 'for letting him go'. y prytwn 'at this time' (pryd hwn). y wlat arall 'to another land': gwlat soft-mutated after y 'to'. onys guahodwn 'unless we invite him': ony 'unless' + infixed s 'him'; guahodwn is the 1st plural present of gwahawd.

sentences.t: “Dioer, Arglwydes,” heb wy, “iawnhaf yw y wahawd.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly, Lady,” said they, “rightest is to-invite-him.”
sentences.i: “Indeed, Lady,” they said, “the right thing is to invite him.”
sentences.n: iawnhaf is the superlative of iawn 'right'. y wahawd 'his inviting': gwahawd soft-mutated after y 'his'. Arglwydes 'Lady' is the form of address to the lord's wife.

sentences.t: Yna yd aeth kennadeu yn y erbyn y wahawd.
sentences.l: Then went messengers to-meet-him to invite-him.
sentences.i: Then messengers went out to meet him and invite him.
sentences.n: yd aeth kennadeu 'went messengers': a singular verb before a plural noun subject is the regular Middle Welsh agreement. kennadeu is the plural of kennat 'messenger'. yn y erbyn 'to meet him' is the compound preposition yn erbyn with y 'his' set inside it.

sentences.t: Ac yna y kymerth ef wahawd yn llawen, ac y doeth y'r llys, ac y doeth hitheu yn y erbyn y graessawu, ac y gyuarch well idaw.
sentences.l: And then took he invitation gladly, and came to the court, and came she-for-her-part to-meet-him to welcome-him, and to greet him.
sentences.i: And then he accepted the invitation gladly and came to the court, and she came out to meet him, to welcome him and to give him greeting.
sentences.n: kymerth is the 3rd singular preterite of kymryt 'take'. wahawd is gwahawd 'invitation', soft-mutated as the object. The White Book has no y before it; the Red Book reads y kymerth ef y wahawd 'took his invitation', and the second witness brackets that y, but the sense stands without it and nothing is supplied. y'r is y 'to' + 'r 'the'. y graessawu 'to welcome him': croessawu (croesawu) soft-mutated after y 'his', written with ae. y gyuarch well idaw 'to greet him': kyuarch gwell i, lit. 'ask better to', soft-mutated after y 'to'; idaw 'to him'.

sentences.t: “Arglwydes, Duw a dalho it dy lywenyd.”
sentences.l: “Lady, God may-he-repay to-you your gladness.”
sentences.i: “Lady, may God repay you for your glad welcome.”
sentences.n: Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you': dalho is talho, the present subjunctive of talu with the older ending -ho, soft-mutated after a. it 'to you' (iti). llywenyd is 'joy, gladness', here the gladness of her welcome. The speaker is Gronw; the White Book has no heb ef here. The second witness brackets [heb ef] from the Red Book; it is not supplied.

sentences.t: Ymdiarchenu, a mynet y eisted a wnaethant.
sentences.l: Unshoeing, and going to sit they-did.
sentences.i: They took off their outdoor things and went to sit down.
sentences.n: Two verbal nouns closed by a wnaethant, the 3rd plural preterite of gwneuthur: 'they took off … and went'. ymdiarchenu is lit. 'unshoe oneself' (archen 'shoe'), to take off travelling gear; y eisted 'to sit' (eistedd).

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth Blodeued, edrych arnaw ef, ac yr awr yd edrych, nit oed gyueir arnei hi ny bei yn llawn o'e garyat ef.
sentences.l: That-is what did Blodeuedd, looking at-him, and the hour that she-looks, there-was-not a-part on-her that was-not full of his love.
sentences.i: Blodeuedd looked at him, and in the moment she looked there was no part of her that was not filled with love for him.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth Blodeued, edrych 'that is what Blodeuedd did, look': sef points ahead to the verbal noun that answers it, and the whole means simply 'Blodeuedd looked'. The scribe writes her name Blodeued here and Blodeuwed later; the English keeps Blodeuedd throughout. yr awr yd edrych 'the hour she looks': the present tense for the vivid moment. gyueir 'part, region' is kyueir soft-mutated after nit oed. arnei 'on her' (ar, 3rd singular feminine). ny bei 'that was not': bei is the imperfect subjunctive of bot in a negative relative clause. o'e garyat ef 'of his love': caryat soft-mutated after 'e 'his'.

sentences.t: Ac ynteu a synywys arnei hitheu; a'r un medwl a doeth yndaw ef ac a doeth yndi hitheu.
sentences.l: And he-for-his-part it-was-that gazed on-her for-her-part; and the same thought came into-him that came into-her.
sentences.i: And he in turn gazed upon her; and the same thought came into him as had come into her.
sentences.n: synywys is the 3rd singular preterite of synnyaw 'notice, look closely', with the -wys ending. a'r un medwl 'and the same thought'. yndaw 'in him' and yndi 'in her' are the preposition yn conjugated.

sentences.t: Ef ny allwys ymgelu o'e uot yn y charu, a'e uenegi idi a wnaeth.
sentences.l: He could-not conceal of his being loving-her, and telling-it to-her he-did.
sentences.i: He could not hide that he loved her, and he told her so.
sentences.n: ny allwys: gallwys, 3rd singular preterite of gallu 'be able', soft-mutated after ny. ymgelu 'conceal (oneself)', from celu. o'e uot 'of his being': bot soft-mutated after 'e 'his'. yn y charu 'loving her': y 'her' causes spirant mutation, caru > charu; contrast a'e uenegi 'and telling it', where 'e 'its' (masculine) causes soft mutation, menegi > uenegi. a wnaeth closes the verbal noun: 'he told'.

sentences.t: Hitheu a gymerth diruawr lywenyd yndi.
sentences.l: She-for-her-part it-was-that took great joy in-her.
sentences.i: And great gladness filled her.
sentences.n: gymerth is kymerth 'took', soft-mutated after a. diruawr 'very great' (dirfawr) stands before its noun and soft-mutates it: llywenyd > lywenyd. yndi 'in her', within herself, as the thought came yndi in the sentence before.

sentences.t: Ac o achaws y serch, a'r caryat, a dodassei pob un o honunt ar y gilyd, y bu eu hymdidan y nos honno.
sentences.l: And because of the desire, and the love, that had-set each one of-them on the other, there-was their conversing that night.
sentences.i: And because of the desire and the love that each of them had set upon the other, they spent that night in talk together.
sentences.n: o achaws 'because of'. dodassei is the pluperfect of dodi 'put, set', with the ending -assei: 'had set'. o honunt 'of them' (o, 3rd plural). ar y gilyd 'on the other'. eu hymdidan 'their conversing': eu 'their' puts h before a vowel. y bu 'there was'.

sentences.t: Ac ny bu ohir e ymgael o honunt, amgen no'r nos honno.
sentences.l: And there-was-not delay to their-getting-each-other by-them, other than that night.
sentences.i: And they did not put off coming together any later than that night.
sentences.n: ohir is gohir 'delay', soft-mutated after bu. e ymgael 'to get one another', the reciprocal ym- with cael. o honunt marks who does it. amgen no 'other than': there was no delay beyond that same night.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno kyscu y gyt a wnaethant.
sentences.l: And that night sleeping together they-did.
sentences.i: And that night they slept together.
sentences.n: kyscu y gyt a wnaethant 'sleeping together they did': the verbal noun closed by a wnaethant. y gyt 'together' (ynghyd).

sentences.t: A thrannoeth, arouun a wnaeth ef e ymdeith.
sentences.l: And next-day, intending he-did to go-away.
sentences.i: And the next day he made ready to leave.
sentences.n: A thrannoeth 'and the next day': trannoeth with spirant mutation after a. arouun a wnaeth 'intending he did': arouun is arofun 'purpose, intend, make ready', closed by a wnaeth. e ymdeith 'to go away': e is y 'to', ymdeith 'away, departure' (ymaith). The subject is Gronw.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb hi, “nyt ey y wrthyf i heno.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said she, “you-will-not-go from-me tonight.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” she said, “you shall not go from me tonight.”
sentences.n: ey is the 2nd singular present of mynet 'go' (modern ei), with future sense. y wrthyf i 'from me': y wrth (oddi wrth) with wrth conjugated for the 1st singular.

sentences.t: E nos honno y buant y gyt heuyt.
sentences.l: That night they-were together also.
sentences.i: That night too they were together.
sentences.n: E nos honno is y nos honno 'that night'; honno is the feminine 'that'. buant is the 3rd plural preterite of bot. heuyt 'also' (hefyd).

sentences.t: A'r nos honno y bu yr ymgynghor ganthunt pa furu y kehynt uot yg kyt.
sentences.l: And that night there-was the taking-counsel by-them what way they-might-get to-be together.
sentences.i: And that night they took counsel together how they might be together for good.
sentences.n: ymgynghor 'taking counsel together', with the reciprocal ym-. ganthunt 'with them' (gan, 3rd plural). pa furu 'in what manner': furu is ffurf 'form, manner', f for ff. kehynt is the 3rd plural imperfect subjunctive of cael, 'they might get'. yg kyt 'together': yng nghyd, the nasal mutation written g + k.

sentences.t: “Nyt oes gynghor it,” heb ef, “onyt un; keissaw y ganthaw gwybot pa furu y del y angheu, a hynny yn rith ymgeled amdanaw.”
sentences.l: “There-is-not counsel to-you,” said he, “but one; seeking from-him to-know what way may-come his death, and that in the-guise of care for-him.”
sentences.i: “There is only one counsel for you,” he said: “to try to learn from him in what way his death may come, and that under the guise of care for him.”
sentences.n: gynghor 'counsel' is kynghor soft-mutated after nyt oes. onyt 'except, but'. keissaw 'seek, try'. y ganthaw 'from him' (gan, 3rd singular masculine, with y). del is the 3rd singular present subjunctive of dyuot 'come'. yn rith 'in the guise of' (rhith 'form, guise'). ymgeled 'care, tending' (ymgeledd). amdanaw 'about him' (am, 3rd singular masculine). The speaker is Gronw.

sentences.t: Trannoeth, arouun a wnaeth.
sentences.l: Next-day, intending he-did.
sentences.i: The next day he made ready to leave.
sentences.n: The same formula as before, arouun a wnaeth 'he made ready to go', here without e ymdeith.

sentences.t: “Dioer, ni chyghoraf it hediw uynet e wrthyf i.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly, I-do-not-counsel to-you today to-go from-me.”
sentences.i: “Indeed, I do not advise you to go from me today.”
sentences.n: Blodeuedd speaks; there is no speech tag. ni chyghoraf 'I do not counsel': kynghoraf, 1st singular present of kynghori, takes spirant mutation after ni, and the scribe writes g for ng (chyghoraf), as he does elsewhere in this part. Evans prints nit with the t dotted beneath, the scribe's mark of deletion, so the word is ni. hediw 'today' (heddiw). uynet is mynet 'go', soft-mutated. e wrthyf i 'from me', as y wrthyf above.

sentences.t: “Dioer, canys kynghory ditheu, nit af inheu,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Assuredly, since you-counsel you-for-your-part, I-will-not-go I-for-my-part,” said he.
sentences.i: “Indeed, since you advise it, I will not go,” he said.
sentences.n: canys 'since, because': in the manuscript the s is written above the line, brought down into it here. kynghory is the 2nd singular present of kynghori. ditheu and inheu are the conjunctive pronouns 'you in your turn', 'I in mine'. af is the 1st singular present of mynet.

sentences.t: “Dywedaf hagen uot yn perigyl dyuot yr unben bieu y llys adref.”
sentences.l: “I-say however being in danger the coming of the chieftain who-owns the court home.”
sentences.i: “I say, though, that there is danger of the chieftain who owns this court coming home.”
sentences.n: Gronw is still speaking. hagen 'however'. uot 'being' (bot, soft-mutated as the object of dywedaf): 'I say that it is …'. yn perigyl 'in danger': perigyl is left unmutated after yn, where the nasal mutation might be expected. bieu 'whose is, who owns'. adref 'home(wards)'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hi, “auory, mi a'th ganhadaf di e ymdeith.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she, “tomorrow I it-is-that will-permit-you to go-away.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “tomorrow I will let you go.”
sentences.n: mi a'th ganhadaf: the abnormal order with mi first; a'th is a + the infixed pronoun 'th 'you', which soft-mutates the verb: kanhadaf > ganhadaf, 1st singular present of kanhadu 'permit, let go' (caniatáu). di repeats 'you'.

sentences.t: Trannoeth, arouun a wnaeth ef, ac ny ludywys hitheu ef.
sentences.l: Next-day, intending he-did, and she-for-her-part did-not-hinder him.
sentences.i: The next day he made ready to leave, and she did not hinder him.
sentences.n: arouun a wnaeth as before. ny ludywys: lludywys, 3rd singular preterite of lludyaw 'hinder', soft-mutated after ny.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “coffa a dywedeis wrthyt, ac ymdidan yn lut ac ef; a hynny yn rith ysmalawch caryat ac ef. A dilyt y gantaw pa ford y gallei dyuot y angheu.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “remember what I-said to-you, and talking closely with him; and that in the-guise of playfulness of-love with him. And drawing from-him what way could come his death.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “remember what I told you, and talk closely with him, and do it under the guise of loving play with him; and draw out of him in what way his death could come.”
sentences.n: Gronw gives his parting instructions. coffa 'remember' is the 2nd singular imperative of coffau (cofio). a dywedeis 'what I said': a is the relative 'that which', dywedeis the 1st singular preterite. wrthyt 'to you'. yn lut 'closely, insistently' is probably glut, gludd 'clinging, persistent', soft-mutated after yn; the word is not certain. ysmalawch 'playfulness, banter' (cf. smala). dilyt 'pursue, follow up, obtain', here 'draw out' of him. gallei is the 3rd singular imperfect of gallu, 'could'.

sentences.t: Enteu a doeth adref y nos honno.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part came home that night.
sentences.i: Lleu came home that night.
sentences.n: Enteu is the scribe's spelling of ynteu 'he for his part'; the subject is Lleu, back from Caer Dathyl. doeth 'came'; adref 'home'.

sentences.t: Treulaw y dyd a wnaethant drwy ymdidan, a cherd, a chyuedach.
sentences.l: Spending the day they-did through talk, and song, and carousal.
sentences.i: They spent the day in talk and song and feasting.
sentences.n: Treulaw y dyd a wnaethant 'spending the day they did': treulaw 'spend' (treulio) closed by a wnaethant. a cherd, a chyuedach: kerd 'song' and kyuedach 'carousal, drinking together' (cyfeddach) with spirant mutation after a.

sentences.t: A'r nos honno y gyscu y gyt yd aethant.
sentences.l: And that night to sleep together went they.
sentences.i: And that night they went to bed together.
sentences.n: y gyscu 'to sleep': kyscu soft-mutated after y 'to'. yd aethant 'they went' (3rd plural preterite of mynet), with yd before the vowel because the sentence does not begin with its subject.

sentences.t: Ac ef a dywot parabyl, a'r eil wrthi.
sentences.l: And he it-was-that spoke a-word, and the second, to-her.
sentences.i: And he said something to her, and then a second thing.
sentences.n: parabyl 'utterance, word' (parabl). a'r eil 'and the second'. wrthi 'to her' (wrth, 3rd singular feminine).

sentences.t: Ac yn hynny parabyl nis cauas.
sentences.l: And in that a-word he-did-not-get-it.
sentences.i: And for all that he did not get a word from her.
sentences.n: The object parabyl stands first and is picked up by the infixed pronoun in nis, ny + s 'it': 'a word, he did not get it'. cauas is the 3rd singular preterite of cael. yn hynny 'in that', i.e. all the while.

sentences.t: “Pa derw yti,” heb ef, “ac a wyt iach di?”
sentences.l: “What befalls to-you,” said he, “and are you well?”
sentences.i: “What ails you,” he said, “and are you well?”
sentences.n: derw is a form of daruot 'happen, befall', commonly taken as its present subjunctive: Pa derw yti 'what is it with you?'. yti 'to you'. a wyt 'are you': the question particle a with wyt, the 2nd singular present of bot.

sentences.t: “Medylyaw yd wyf,” heb hi, “yr hynn ny medylyut ti amdanaf i. Sef yw hynny,” heb hi, “goualu am dy angheu di, ot elut yn gynt no miui.”
sentences.l: “Thinking I-am,” said she, “that which you-would-not-think about-me. That-is is that,” said she, “worrying about your death, if you-should-go sooner than me.”
sentences.i: “I am thinking,” she said, “of what you would never think of me: that is,” she said, “I am anxious about your death, if you should go before me.”
sentences.n: Medylyaw yd wyf 'thinking I am': the verbal noun is put first for weight and the verb follows with yd. yr hynn 'that which'. ny medylyut is the 2nd singular imperfect of medylyaw, used as a conditional, 'you would not think'. amdanaf 'about me' (am, 1st singular). Sef yw hynny 'that is to say'. goualu 'be anxious, care' (gofalu). ot elut 'if you should go': ot is o 'if' before a vowel, and elut the 2nd singular imperfect subjunctive of mynet. yn gynt 'sooner': kynt soft-mutated after adverbial yn. miui is the reduplicated pronoun 'me'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “Duw a dalho it dy ymgeled. Ony'm llad i Duw hagen, nit hawd uy llad i,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “God may-he-repay to-you your care. Unless-me kills God however, it-is-not easy my killing,” said he.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “may God repay you your care. But unless God kills me, I am not easily killed,” he said.
sentences.n: Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you', as before; ymgeled 'care' (ymgeledd), the word Gronw told her to use as her cover. Ony'm is ony 'unless' + the infixed 'm 'me'; llad is the 3rd singular present 'kills'. uy llad 'my killing': uy is fy 'my'; ll shows no mutation.

sentences.t: “A wney ditheu yr Duw ac yrof inheu, menegi ymi ba furu y galler dy lad ditheu? Canys guell uyghof i wrth ymoglyt no'r teu di.”
sentences.l: “Will-you-do, you-for-your-part, for God and for-me, telling to-me what way can-be-killed you? Since better my-memory for guarding than yours.”
sentences.i: “Will you, for God's sake and for mine, tell me in what way you could be killed? For my memory is better at keeping watch than yours.”
sentences.n: A wney 'will you do': the question particle a with gwney, 2nd singular present of gwneuthur, soft-mutated. yr Duw 'for God'; yrof 'for me' (yr = er, 1st singular). ymi 'to me'. ba furu is pa furu 'what manner', soft-mutated as the object of menegi. y galler is the impersonal present subjunctive of gallu, 'one may'. dy lad: llad soft-mutated after dy. uyghof is fy nghof 'my memory': kof with nasal mutation after uy, the scribe writing g for ng as in chyghoraf. wrth ymoglyt 'for being on guard' (ymogelyd). no'r teu di 'than yours' (teu 'yours').

sentences.t: “Dywedaf yn llawen,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I-will-tell gladly,” said he.
sentences.i: “I will tell you gladly,” he said.
sentences.n: Dywedaf is the 1st singular present of dywedut, used as a future. yn llawen 'gladly'.

sentences.t: “Nit hawd uy llad i,” heb ef, “o ergyt. A reit oed uot blwydyn yn gwneuthur y par y'm byrhit i ac ef, a heb gwneuthur dim o honaw, namyn pan uythit ar yr aberth duw Sul.”
sentences.l: “It-is-not easy my killing,” said he, “by a-cast. And needful was being a-year making the spear that-I-would-be-struck with it, and without making any of-it, except when one-would-be at the sacrifice on-Sunday.”
sentences.i: “I am not easily killed,” he said, “by any cast. A year would have to be spent making the spear I should be struck with, and no part of it made except while folk were at Mass on Sunday.”
sentences.n: ergyt is a 'cast, shot', the throw of a weapon (house 'blow' is kept for dyrnawt). A reit oed 'and needful would be': oed, the imperfect, does duty for a conditional. y'm byrhit 'that I would be struck': y with the infixed 'm 'me' and byrhit, the impersonal imperfect of bwrw 'throw, strike'; the form is the White Book's, kept as written. heb gwneuthur 'without making': gwneuthur is left unmutated after heb. o honaw 'of it'. pan uythit 'when one would be': bythit, impersonal imperfect of bot, soft-mutated after pan. yr aberth 'the sacrifice' is the Mass; duw Sul 'Sunday', with duw the old word for 'day'.

sentences.t: “Ae diogel hynny?” heb hi.
sentences.l: “Is certain that?” said she.
sentences.i: “Is that certain?” she said.
sentences.n: Ae is the question particle before a word that is not a verb: 'is it certain, that?'

sentences.t: “Diogel, dioer,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “Certain, assuredly,” said he.
sentences.i: “Certain, indeed,” he said.
sentences.n: The answer repeats the word asked about, Diogel 'certain', as Welsh answers do.

sentences.t: “Ny ellir uy llad i y mywn ty,” heb ef, “ny ellir allan; ny ellir uy llad ar uarch, ny ellir ar uyn troet.”
sentences.l: “One-cannot kill me in a-house,” said he, “one-cannot outside; one-cannot kill me on a-horse, one-cannot on my foot.”
sentences.i: “I cannot be killed inside a house,” he said, “nor out of doors; I cannot be killed on horseback, nor on foot.”
sentences.n: ellir is gellir, the impersonal present of gallu 'one can', soft-mutated after ny. y mywn 'within' (i mewn). ar uarch: march 'horse' soft-mutated after ar. ar uyn troet 'on my foot': the nasal mutation after fy is shown in the possessive (uyn) and not on the noun, which would be nhroet.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hitheu, “pa delw y gellit dy lad ditheu?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she-for-her-part, “what way could-one kill you, then?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “then in what way could you be killed?”
sentences.n: pa delw 'in what manner': delw 'form, image', here 'way'. gellit is the impersonal imperfect of gallu, 'one could'. dy lad 'your killing' (llad soft after dy); ditheu 'you, then'.

sentences.t: “Mi a'e dywedaf yti,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “I it-is-that will-tell-it to-you,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “I will tell you,” he said.
sentences.n: Mi a'e dywedaf: the abnormal order, with the infixed 'e 'it' between a and the verb. yti 'to you'.

sentences.t: “Gwneuthur ennein im ar lan auon, a gwneuthur cromglwyt uch benn y gerwyn, a'y thoi yn da didos wedy hynny hyhitheu.
sentences.l: “Making a-bath for-me on the bank of a-river, and making a-curved-hurdle over the head of the tub, and roofing-it well and tight after that, it-for-its-part.
sentences.i: “A bath must be made for me on a river bank, and a curved frame of wattle set over the tub, and that frame then roofed well and tight.
sentences.n: Lleu describes the conditions in verbal nouns, with no finite verb. ennein 'bath' (enaint, also 'ointment'); im 'for me'. ar lan: glan 'bank' soft-mutated after ar. cromglwyt 'curved hurdle', crwm + clwyd, a frame of wattle. uch benn 'above' (uwch ben), penn soft-mutated. y gerwyn 'the tub': kerwyn is feminine, soft after the article. a'y thoi 'and roofing it': y 'its' (feminine, for the clwyt) causes spirant mutation, toi > thoi. yn da didos 'well and weathertight' (didos 'without a leak'). Evans writes wedy (6edẏ) where the second witness has wedi, and prints hy hitheu as two words; it is written hyhitheu, the reduplicated feminine pronoun, 'it (the hurdle) in its turn'. The Red Book has no hyhitheu here.

sentences.t: A dwyn bwch,” heb ef, “a'y dodi gyr llaw y gerwyn, a dodi ohonof uinheu y neill troet ar geuyn y bwch, a'r llall ar emyl y gerwyn. Pwy bynnac a'm metrei i yuelly, ef a wnay uy agheu.”
sentences.l: And bringing a-he-goat,” said he, “and putting-it beside the tub, and putting by-me myself the one foot on the back of the goat, and the other on the edge of the tub. Whoever might-hit me thus, he it-is-that would-make my death.”
sentences.i: And a he-goat must be brought,” he said, “and set beside the tub, and I must put one foot on the goat's back and the other on the edge of the tub. Whoever struck me so would be the death of me.”
sentences.n: bwch 'he-goat, buck'. gyr llaw 'beside' is the scribe's form of ger llaw. ohonof uinheu 'by me myself' marks who does the putting. y neill troet 'the one foot'; ar geuyn: keuyn 'back' soft-mutated after ar. emyl 'edge' (ymyl). a'm metrei 'who might hit me': a'm is a + the infixed 'm 'me', and metrei the 3rd singular imperfect subjunctive of medru 'hit (a mark)'. yuelly 'thus' (felly). wnay is gwnay 'does, will do'. uy agheu 'my death': Evans prints agheu with no n, the scribe's g for ng again; read angheu.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb hitheu, “diolchaf y Duw hynny. Ef a ellir rac hynny dianc yn hawd.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said she-for-her-part, “I-thank God for-that. It it-is-that can-be from that escaping easily.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” she said, “I thank God for that. That can easily be escaped.”
sentences.n: diolchaf y Duw 'I give thanks to God'. Ef a ellir 'it can be': ef is an empty subject and ellir the impersonal present of gallu, soft after a. rac hynny 'from that'; dianc 'escape'.

sentences.t: Nyt kynt noc y cauas hi yr ymadrawd, noc y hanuones hitheu at Gronw Pebyr.
sentences.l: Not sooner than got she the saying, than sent she-for-her-part to Gronw Pebyr.
sentences.i: No sooner had she got the words out of him than she sent to Gronw Pebyr.
sentences.n: Nyt kynt noc … noc 'no sooner than … than'. cauas 'got' (cael). ymadrawd 'speech, saying'. y hanuones 'she sent': anuones is the 3rd singular preterite of anuon 'send'; the h before it is probably the infixed pronoun y 'it' (the message), which puts h before a vowel, though a plain preverbal y may be meant.

sentences.t: Gronw a lauurywys gueith y guayw, a'r un dyd ym penn y ulwydyn y bu barawt.
sentences.l: Gronw it-was-that laboured the work of the spear, and the same day at the end of the year it-was ready.
sentences.i: Gronw laboured at the making of the spear, and on the very day the year came round it was ready.
sentences.n: lauurywys is llauurywys, 3rd singular preterite of llauuryaw 'labour', soft-mutated after a. gueith y guayw 'the work of the spear' (gwaith, gwayw). ym penn y ulwydyn 'at the head of the year': blwydyn is feminine and soft-mutated after the article. barawt is parawt 'ready', soft-mutated after bu. The year is the one Lleu named.

sentences.t: A'r dyd hwnnw y peris ef idi hi guybot hynny.
sentences.l: And that day caused he to-her her knowing that.
sentences.i: And on that day he let her know it.
sentences.n: peris is the 3rd singular preterite of peri 'cause': 'he caused her to know'. idi hi 'to her'. guybot 'know': Evans prints a dot beneath the o (guẏbọt, zoom 12). Elsewhere such a dot marks a letter for deletion, but leaving the o out gives no word, so guybot is kept (the Red Book has gwybot); what the dot means is uncertain.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb hi, “yd wyf yn medylyaw pa delw y gallei uot yn hynn a dywedeisti gynt wrthyf i. Ac a dangossy di ymi pa furu y sauut ti ar emyl y gerwyn a'r bwch, o faraf uinheu yr enneint?”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said she, “I-am thinking what way could be [yn hynn] what you-told before to-me. And will-you-show you to-me what way you-would-stand on the edge of the tub and the goat, if I-have-made-ready I-for-my-part the bath?”
sentences.i: “Lord,” she said, “I am wondering how what you told me the other day could be so. Will you show me how you would stand on the edge of the tub and on the goat, if I have the bath made ready?”
sentences.n: yd wyf yn medylyaw 'I am thinking'. pa delw y gallei uot 'how it could be'. Evans certainly prints yn hynn here (zoom 12); the second witness has yr hynn and the Red Book uot yn wir a dywedeist 'be true, what you said'. yn hynn is probably a slip, either for yr hynn 'that which' or for half of the Red Book's yn wir; the reading is uncertain, and the English follows the sense both share. dywedeisti is dywedeist 'you said' with ti fused on. gynt 'formerly'. dangossy is the 2nd singular present of dangos 'show'. sauut is the 2nd singular imperfect of sefyll 'stand', 'you would stand'. o faraf 'if I cause': paraf, 1st singular present of peri, with spirant mutation after o 'if' (written f). enneint, with t, is the same word as ennein 'bath'.

sentences.t: “Dangossaf,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “I-will-show,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “I will,” he said.
sentences.n: Dangossaf 'I will show': the answer repeats the verb of the question, in the 1st singular.

sentences.t: Hitheu a anuones at Gronw, ac a erchis idaw bot yg kyscawt y brynn a elwir weithon Brynn Kyuergyr.
sentences.l: She-for-her-part it-was-that sent to Gronw, and that bade to-him being in the shelter of the hill that is-called now Bryn Cyfergyr.
sentences.i: She sent to Gronw and bade him be in the shelter of the hill that is now called Bryn Cyfergyr.
sentences.n: erchis is the 3rd singular preterite of erchi 'ask, bid'. idaw 'to him'. yg kyscawt 'in the shelter, the shadow' (yng nghysgod), the nasal mutation written g + k. a elwir is the relative a with gelwir, impersonal present of galw 'call', soft-mutated. weithon 'now' (weithian). The name Bryn Cyfergyr is 'hill of the clash, the onset' (kyuergyr); the text writes Brynn here and Bryn once below.

sentences.t: Y glan Auon Kynuael oed hynny.
sentences.l: On the bank of the River Cynfael was that.
sentences.i: That was on the bank of the river Cynfael.
sentences.n: Evans prints yglan as one word; it is written y glan, as in part 007, where yg and ym before the next word are written y. It stands for yng nglan 'on the bank'. Kynuael is here written unmutated after Auon.

sentences.t: Hitheu a beris kynnullaw a gauas o auyr yn y cantref a'y dwyn o'r parth draw y auon, gyuarwyneb a Bryn Kyuergyr.
sentences.l: She-for-her-part it-was-that caused gathering what she-got of goats in the cantref and bringing-them from the side yonder to river, facing Bryn Cyfergyr.
sentences.i: She had every goat she could find in the cantref gathered and brought to the far side of the river, facing Bryn Cyfergyr.
sentences.n: beris is peris 'caused', soft-mutated after a: 'she had (them) gathered'. kynnullaw 'gather' (cynnull). a gauas 'what she got'. o auyr 'of goats': gauyr, the plural of gafr (modern geifr), soft-mutated after o. a'y dwyn 'and bringing them'. o'r parth draw y auon: Evans has y auon, not y'r auon as the second witness reads (the Red Book has the article), so the White Book says 'to the far side to river', without 'the'; the English supplies nothing. gyuarwyneb a 'opposite, facing' (cyferbyn). Bryn is written with one n here, as Evans prints it.

sentences.t: A thrannoeth hi a dywot, “Arglwyd,” heb hi, “mi a bereis kyweiraw y glwyt, a'r ennein, ac y maent yn barawt.”
sentences.l: And next-day she it-was-that said, “Lord,” said she, “I it-is-that caused making-ready the hurdle, and the bath, and they-are ready.”
sentences.i: And the next day she said, “Lord, I have had the frame and the bath made ready, and all is prepared.”
sentences.n: hi a dywot … heb hi: the speech is introduced twice, by the verb and by the tag, as often. mi a bereis 'I caused': bereis is pereis, 1st singular preterite of peri, soft after a. kyweiraw 'prepare, set in order' (cyweirio). y glwyt: clwyt is feminine, soft-mutated after the article. maent 'they are'; yn barawt: parawt soft after yn.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “awn eu hedrych yn llawen.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “let-us-go their seeing gladly.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “let us go and look at them, and gladly.”
sentences.n: awn is the 1st plural of mynet, 'let us go'. eu hedrych 'to see them': eu 'their' puts h before the vowel.

sentences.t: Wy a doethant trannoeth y edrych yr enneint.
sentences.l: They it-was-that came next-day to look-at the bath.
sentences.i: They came the next day to look at the bath.
sentences.n: doethant is the 3rd plural preterite of dyuot 'come'. y edrych 'to look at'.

sentences.t: “Ti a ey y'r ennein, Arglwyd?” heb hi.
sentences.l: “You it-is-that will-go to the bath, Lord?” said she.
sentences.i: “Will you go into the bath, Lord?” she said.
sentences.n: Ti a ey 'you will go': a statement in the abnormal order, made a question by the voice.

sentences.t: “Af yn llawen,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I-will-go gladly,” said he.
sentences.i: “I will, gladly,” he said.
sentences.n: Af 'I will go' answers ey 'will you go'.

sentences.t: Ef a aeth y'r ennein, ac ymneinaw a wnaeth.
sentences.l: He it-was-that went into the bath, and bathing he-did.
sentences.i: He went into the bath and bathed.
sentences.n: ymneinaw 'bathe oneself': ym- with eneinaw 'anoint, bathe'. a wnaeth closes the verbal noun.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb hi, “llyma yr aniueileit a dywedeisti uot bwch arnunt.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said she, “here-are the animals that you-said being 'bwch' on-them.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” she said, “here are the animals you said were called goats.”
sentences.n: llyma 'here are'. aniueileit is a plural of aniueil 'animal'. uot bwch arnunt 'that bwch was on them', that is, that they bore the name bwch. arnunt 'on them' (ar, 3rd plural).

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “par dala un ohonunt, a phar y dwyn yma.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “have catching one of-them, and have its bringing here.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “have one of them caught and brought here.”
sentences.n: par is the 2nd singular imperative of peri 'cause, have (something) done'; a phar shows spirant mutation after a. dala 'catch' (dal). ohonunt 'of them'. y dwyn 'its bringing'.

sentences.t: Ef a ducpwyt.
sentences.l: It it-was-that was-brought.
sentences.i: It was brought.
sentences.n: ducpwyt is the impersonal preterite of dwyn 'bring'.

sentences.t: Yna y kyuodes ynteu o'r ennein a guiscaw y lawdyr amdanaw, ac y dodes y neilltroet ar emyl y gerwyn, a'r llall ar geuyn y bwch.
sentences.l: Then rose he-for-his-part from the bath and putting-on his breeches about-him, and set the one-foot on the edge of the tub, and the other on the back of the goat.
sentences.i: Then he rose from the bath and put on his breeches, and set one foot on the edge of the tub and the other on the goat's back.
sentences.n: kyuodes is the 3rd singular preterite of kyuodi 'rise'. guiscaw 'put on, dress' (gwisgo). y lawdyr 'his breeches': llawdyr soft-mutated after y 'his'. dodes 'set' is the preterite of dodi. neilltroet 'one foot' is written as one word here.

sentences.t: Ynteu Gronw a gyuodes e uynyd o'r brynn a elwir Brynn Kyuergyr, ac ar benn y neill glin y kyuodes, ac a'r guenwynwayw y uwrw, a'y uedru yn y ystlys, yny neita y paladyr ohonaw, a thrigyaw y penn yndaw.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Gronw it-was-that rose up from the hill that is-called Bryn Cyfergyr, and on top of the one knee he-rose, and with the poison-spear casting-at-him, and hitting-him in his side, so-that sprang the shaft from-it, and staying the head in-him.
sentences.i: Gronw rose up from the hill that is called Bryn Cyfergyr, and rose on to one knee, and cast at him with the poisoned spear and struck him in the side, so that the shaft sprang out of it and the head stayed in him.
sentences.n: e uynyd 'up' (i fyny). ar benn y neill glin 'on top of the one knee': glin soft-mutated after neill. a'r guenwynwayw 'with the poison-spear', a compound of gwenwyn 'poison' and gwayw 'spear', the second element soft-mutated. y uwrw 'to cast at him': bwrw soft-mutated after y 'him'. a'y uedru 'and hitting him': medru soft-mutated. ystlys 'side'. yny 'so that, until'. neita is the 3rd singular imperfect of neidyaw 'leap'. paladyr 'shaft'. a thrigyaw 'and staying': trigyaw with spirant mutation after a. y penn 'the head' of the spear.

sentences.t: Ac yna bwrw ehetuan o honaw ynteu yn rith eryr, a dodi garymleis anhygar.
sentences.l: And then casting a-flight by-him, him-for-his-part, in the-form of an-eagle, and giving a-harsh-cry unlovely.
sentences.i: And then Lleu took flight in the form of an eagle and gave a hideous scream.
sentences.n: bwrw ehetuan 'cast a flight', i.e. fly up (ehedfan). o honaw ynteu 'by him in his turn' marks Lleu as the doer. yn rith eryr 'in the form of an eagle'. garymleis 'harsh cry, scream' is a rare compound, apparently garw 'rough' with a form of llais 'voice'; its make-up is not certain. anhygar 'unlovely, repellent' (an- + hygar 'amiable'); Evans prints it as two words, an hẏgar.

sentences.t: Ac ny chahat y welet ef odyna y maes.
sentences.l: And there-was-not-had his seeing from-there out.
sentences.i: And from then on he was not seen.
sentences.n: ny chahat 'there was not got': cahat, the impersonal preterite of cael, with spirant mutation after ny. y welet ef 'his seeing': gwelet soft-mutated after y 'his'. odyna y maes 'from there out', i.e. after that.

sentences.t: Yn gyn gyflymet ac yd aeth ef e ymdeith, y kyrchyssant wynteu y llys, a'r nos honno kyscu y gyt.
sentences.l: As swift as went he away, they-made-for, they-for-their-part, the court, and that night sleeping together.
sentences.i: As soon as he was gone, they made for the court, and that night they slept together.
sentences.n: Yn gyn gyflymet ac 'as swift as': the equative kyflymet 'as swift' (kyflym + -et), with kyn before it and the soft mutation it causes; Evans prints the phrase as one word. kyrchyssant is the 3rd plural preterite of kyrchu 'make for', with the ending -yssant. wynteu 'they in their turn'.

sentences.t: A thrannoeth kyuodi a oruc Gronw, a guereskyn Ardudwy.
sentences.l: And next-day rising did Gronw, and conquering Ardudwy.
sentences.i: And the next day Gronw rose and took possession of Ardudwy.
sentences.n: kyuodi a oruc 'rising he did': oruc, preterite of gwneuthur, closes the verbal noun as a wnaeth does. guereskyn 'conquer, take possession of' (goresgyn); the next sentence spells it gwreskyn. Ardudwy is Lleu's land on the coast of Meirionnydd.

sentences.t: Guedy gwreskyn y wlat, y gwledychu a wnaeth yny oed yn y eidaw ef Ardudwy a Phenllyn.
sentences.l: After conquering the land, ruling-it he-did until was in his possession Ardudwy and Penllyn.
sentences.i: When he had conquered the land, he ruled it, until both Ardudwy and Penllyn were his.
sentences.n: Guedy 'after' (wedi). y wlat: gwlat soft-mutated after the article. y gwledychu 'its ruling': y here is 'it', the land, and does not mutate g. yn y eidaw ef 'in his possession' (eiddo). a Phenllyn: Penllyn with spirant mutation after a. Gronw now holds his own land and Lleu's.

sentences.t: Yna y chwedyl a aeth at Math uab Mathonwy.
sentences.l: Then the tidings it-was-that went to Math son of Mathonwy.
sentences.i: Then the tidings went to Math son of Mathonwy.
sentences.n: chwedyl 'tale, tidings' (chwedl). After the adverb yna the subject still comes before a and the verb.

sentences.t: Trymuryt a goueileint a gymerth Math yndaw, a mwy Wydyon noc ynteu lawer.
sentences.l: Heavy-heart and grief it-was-that took Math in-him, and more Gwydion than he much.
sentences.i: Math took heaviness of heart and grief to himself, and Gwydion far more than he.
sentences.n: Trymuryt 'heaviness of mind, sorrow' (trwm + bryd), written as one word with the second witness; Evans prints Tzẏm urẏt as two. goueileint 'grief, anxiety' (gofeiliant). gymerth Math yndaw 'Math took into himself': the object stands first, the subject after the verb. Wydyon is Gwydion, Lleu's uncle, soft-mutated in this elliptical clause. noc ynteu 'than he'; lawer 'by much' (llawer, soft-mutated as an adverb).

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Guydyon, “ny orffwyssaf uyth, yny gaffwyf chwedleu y wrth uy nei.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Gwydion, “I-will-not-rest ever, until I-get tidings of my nephew.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Gwydion, “I shall never rest until I have news of my nephew.”
sentences.n: heb y is the form of the tag before a name. ny orffwyssaf: gorffwyssaf, 1st singular present of gorffwys 'rest', soft-mutated after ny. uyth 'ever' (byth). yny gaffwyf 'until I get': caffwyf, 1st singular present subjunctive of cael, soft after yny. y wrth 'from, about'. nei 'nephew' (nai).

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb y Math, “Duw a uo nerth yt.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said Math, “God may-he-be strength to-you.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” said Math, “God be your strength.”
sentences.n: a uo: bo, the present subjunctive of bot, soft-mutated after a, 'may he be'. nerth 'strength'. yt 'to you'.

sentences.t: Ac yna kychwynnu a wnaeth ef, a dechreu rodyaw racdaw, a rodyaw Gwyned a wnaeth, a Phowys yn y theruyn.
sentences.l: And then setting-out he-did, and beginning to-wander onward, and wandering Gwynedd he-did, and Powys to its bounds.
sentences.i: And then he set out and began to wander onward, and he wandered through Gwynedd, and Powys to its furthest bounds.
sentences.n: kychwynnu a wnaeth 'he set out'. rodyaw 'wander, travel about' (rhodio). racdaw 'before him, onward' (rhag, 3rd singular masculine). a Phowys: spirant mutation after a. yn y theruyn 'to its bound': y 'its', feminine, causes spirant mutation, teruyn > theruyn.

sentences.t: Guedy rodyaw pob lle, ef a doeth y Aruon, ac a doeth y ty uab eillt, y Maynawr Bennard.
sentences.l: After wandering every place, he came to Arfon, and came to the house of a-bondman, in Maenor Bennardd.
sentences.i: When he had wandered every place he came to Arfon, and to the house of a bondman at Maenor Bennardd.
sentences.n: Aruon is Arfon, the cantref facing Môn. uab eillt 'son of a villein', a bondman, a tied tenant (mab, soft-mutated). y Maynawr Bennard 'in Maenor Bennardd': y probably stands for ym before the m, as yg is written y above; Bennard is Pennard soft-mutated after the feminine maenor.

sentences.t: Diskynnu yn y ty a wnaeth, a thrigyaw yno y nos honno.
sentences.l: Alighting at the house he-did, and staying there that night.
sentences.i: He alighted at the house and stayed there that night.
sentences.n: Diskynnu 'dismount, alight' closed by a wnaeth; a thrigyaw 'and staying', trigyaw with spirant mutation after a.

sentences.t: Gwr y ty a'y dylwyth a doeth ymywn, ac yn diwethaf y doeth y meichat.
sentences.l: The man of the house and his household it-was-that came in, and last came the swineherd.
sentences.i: The master of the house and his household came in, and last of all came the swineherd.
sentences.n: a'y dylwyth 'and his household': tylwyth soft-mutated after y 'his'. doeth is singular though the subject is two people, the usual agreement in the abnormal sentence. ymywn 'in'. yn diwethaf 'last'. meichat 'swineherd' (meichiad).

sentences.t: Gwr y ty a dywot wrth y meichat, “A was,” heb ef, “a doeth dy hwch di heno y mywn?”
sentences.l: The man of the house it-was-that said to the swineherd, “O lad,” said he, “did-come your sow in tonight?”
sentences.i: The master of the house said to the swineherd, “Lad, has your sow come in tonight?”
sentences.n: A was 'O lad': the vocative particle a, with gwas soft-mutated. a doeth 'did (she) come?': the question particle a with the verb. hwch 'sow'. y mywn 'in'.

sentences.t: “Doeth,” heb ynteu, “yr awr honn y doeth at y moch.”
sentences.l: “She-came,” said he-for-his-part, “this hour she-came to the pigs.”
sentences.i: “She has,” he said; “she came in to the pigs just now.”
sentences.n: Doeth 'came': the answer repeats the verb, the Welsh way of saying 'yes'. yr awr honn 'this hour', just now. moch 'pigs'.

sentences.t: “Ba ryw gerdet,” heb y Guydyon, “yssyd ar yr hwch honno?”
sentences.l: “What kind-of going,” said Gwydion, “is on that sow?”
sentences.i: “What sort of going about,” said Gwydion, “does that sow have?”
sentences.n: Ba ryw is the scribe's form of pa ryw 'what kind'. gerdet 'going' is kerdet soft-mutated after ryw. yssyd 'which is'.

sentences.t: “Ban agorer y creu beunyd yd a allan. Ny cheir craf arnei, ac ni wybydir ba ford yd a, mwy no chyn elei yn y daear.”
sentences.l: “When is-opened the sty every-day, she-goes out. There-is-not-got hold on-her, and it-is-not-known what way she-goes, more than as-if she-went into the earth.”
sentences.i: “Every day when the sty is opened, out she goes. No one can lay hold of her, and no one knows which way she goes, any more than if she went into the earth.”
sentences.n: The swineherd answers; there is no tag. Ban is pan 'when'. agorer is the impersonal present subjunctive of agori 'open'. creu 'sty, pen' (crau). beunyd 'every day'. yd a 'she goes': a is the 3rd singular present of mynet. Ny cheir: ceir, the impersonal present of cael, with spirant mutation after ny. craf 'grip, hold'. ac ni wybydir: Evans prints ni here, the second witness ny; wybydir is gwybydir, impersonal present of gwybot, soft after ni. mwy no 'any more than'. chyn is kyn 'as if', with spirant mutation after no. elei is the 3rd singular imperfect subjunctive of mynet.

sentences.t: “A wney di,” heb y Guydyon, “yrof i, nat agorych y creu yny uwyf i yn y neillparth y'r creu y gyt a thi?”
sentences.l: “Will-you-do,” said Gwydion, “for-me, that you-open-not the sty until I-be on the one-side of the sty together with you?”
sentences.i: “Will you do this for me,” said Gwydion: “not open the sty until I am beside it with you?”
sentences.n: A wney di 'will you do'. yrof i 'for me' (Evans writes yrofi; divided as in part 001). nat agorych 'that you do not open': agorych, 2nd singular present subjunctive of agori, after nat. yny uwyf 'until I be': bwyf, 1st singular present subjunctive of bot, soft after yny. y neillparth 'the one side', beside. a thi 'with you': ti with spirant mutation after a.

sentences.t: “Gwnaf yn llawen,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I-will-do gladly,” said he.
sentences.i: “I will, gladly,” he said.
sentences.n: Gwnaf 'I will do' answers wney 'will you do'.

sentences.t: Y gyscu yd aethant y nos honno.
sentences.l: To sleep went they that night.
sentences.i: They went to sleep that night.
sentences.n: Y gyscu 'to sleep' (kyscu soft after y 'to') stands first, as in the same phrase earlier, and yd aethant follows.

sentences.t: A phan welas y meichat lliw y dyd, ef a deffroes Wydyon, a chyuodi a wnaeth Gwydyon, a guiscaw amdanaw a dyuot y gyt a seuyll wrth y creu.
sentences.l: And when saw the swineherd the colour of the day, he it-was-that woke Gwydion, and rising did Gwydion, and dressing about-him and coming together and standing by the sty.
sentences.i: And when the swineherd saw the light of day he woke Gwydion, and Gwydion rose and dressed and came with him and stood by the sty.
sentences.n: welas is gwelas, 3rd singular preterite of gwelet, soft after pan. lliw y dyd 'the colour of the day', daylight. deffroes 'woke' (deffroi); Wydyon is Gwydion soft-mutated as the object. guiscaw amdanaw 'dressing about him', putting on his clothes. y gyt 'together': the White Book does not say with whom; the second witness adds [ac ef] 'with him', which is not supplied. seuyll 'stand' (sefyll).

sentences.t: Y meichat a agores y creu.
sentences.l: The swineherd it-was-that opened the sty.
sentences.i: The swineherd opened the sty.
sentences.n: agores is the 3rd singular preterite of agori 'open'.

sentences.t: Y gyt ac y hegyr, llyma hitheu yn bwrw neit allan, a cherdet yn braf a wnaeth, a Guydyon a'y canlynwys.
sentences.l: As-soon-as he-opens-it, behold her casting a-leap out, and going swiftly she-did, and Gwydion it-was-that followed-her.
sentences.i: As soon as he opened it, out she leapt and went off at a fine pace, and Gwydion followed her.
sentences.n: Y gyt ac 'as soon as'. y hegyr: egyr is the 3rd singular present of agori 'opens' (the a becomes e), and the h is probably that of the infixed pronoun y 'it', the sty: 'as he opens it'. llyma hitheu 'behold her'. bwrw neit 'cast a leap', leap. yn braf 'strongly, at a fine pace'; the exact sense of braf here is uncertain. a'y canlynwys 'followed her': a + infixed y 'her', and canlynwys, 3rd singular preterite of canlyn 'follow'.

sentences.t: A chymryt gwrthwyneb auon a wnaeth, a chyrchu nant a wnaeth, a elwir weithon Nantllew, ac yna guastatau a wnaeth, a phori.
sentences.l: And taking against the river she-did, and making-for a-valley she-did, that is-called now Nantlleu, and then halting she-did, and grazing.
sentences.i: She went up against the stream and made for a valley that is now called Nantlleu, and there she slowed and grazed.
sentences.n: A chymryt: kymryt with spirant mutation after a. gwrthwyneb auon 'the opposite of the river', upstream. nant 'valley, stream'. a elwir weithon 'which is now called'. Nantllew, written as one word (Evans nantlle6), is Nantlleu, 'Lleu's valley' in Arfon, named in this story. guastatau 'level off, settle, come to a stand' (gwastatáu). a phori 'and grazing': pori with spirant mutation after a.

sentences.t: Ynteu Wydyon a doeth y dan y prenn, ac a edrychwys pa beth yd oed yr hwch yn y bori; ac ef a welei yr hwch yn pori kic pwdyr a chynron.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Gwydion it-was-that came under the tree, and that looked what thing was the sow grazing; and he it-was-that saw the sow grazing rotten flesh and maggots.
sentences.i: Gwydion came beneath the tree and looked to see what the sow was feeding on; and he saw the sow eating rotten flesh and maggots.
sentences.n: Ynteu Wydyon: the name is soft-mutated after ynteu. y dan 'under' (o dan). y prenn 'the tree': the tale speaks of 'the tree' though none has been mentioned, as if the hearer already knew it. edrychwys is the 3rd singular preterite of edrych 'look'. pa beth 'what thing': peth soft after pa. yn y bori 'grazing it': y 'it' with pori soft-mutated. ef a welei 'he saw', the imperfect of gwelet. kic pwdyr 'rotten flesh' (cig pwdr). a chynron: kynron 'maggots' (cynrhon) with spirant mutation after a.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ynteu, edrych ym blaen y prenn.
sentences.l: That-is what did he-for-his-part, looking into the top of the tree.
sentences.i: And he looked up into the top of the tree.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth ynteu, edrych: the sef pattern, 'he looked'. ym blaen 'in the top' (ym mlaen), the nasal mutation after yn shown only in the preposition. Evans prints blen with a small a written above it; the raised letter is brought into the line, blaen.

sentences.t: A phan edrych, ef a welei eryr ym blaen y prenn.
sentences.l: And when he-looks, he it-was-that saw an-eagle in the top of the tree.
sentences.i: And as he looked, he saw an eagle in the top of the tree.
sentences.n: A phan edrych 'and when he looks': the present tense again for the moment of seeing. eryr 'eagle'.

sentences.t: A phan ymyskytwei yr eryr, y syrthei y pryuet a'r kic pwdyr o honaw, a'r hwch yn yssu y rei hynny.
sentences.l: And when shook-itself the eagle, there-fell the vermin and the rotten flesh from-it, and the sow devouring those.
sentences.i: And whenever the eagle shook itself, the worms and the rotten flesh fell from it, and the sow was devouring them.
sentences.n: ymyskytwei is the 3rd singular imperfect of ymysgwyd 'shake oneself'; syrthei, the imperfect of syrthyaw 'fall'. The imperfects describe what kept happening. pryuet 'worms, vermin' (pryfed). yssu 'devour' (ysu). y rei hynny 'those ones'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ynteu, medylyaw y mae Lleu oed yr eryr, a chanu englyn: “Dar a dyf y rwng deu lenn, Gorduwrych awyr a glenn. Ony dywedaf i eu, O ulodeu Lleu ban yw hynn.”
sentences.l: That-is what did he-for-his-part, thinking that it-is Lleu was the eagle, and singing an-englyn: “An-oak that-grows between two glens(?), Very-dark(?) sky and glen. Unless I-speak falsely, From the flowers of Lleu whence is this(?).”
sentences.i: And he thought that the eagle was Lleu, and sang an englyn: “An oak grows between two glens; dark are the sky and the glen. Unless I speak falsely, this comes of Lleu's flowers.”
sentences.n: medylyaw y mae Lleu oed yr eryr 'thinking that it was Lleu the eagle was': y mae (modern mai) introduces the clause with Lleu put first. Here and in the englynion the name is written Lleu. a chanu: kanu 'sing' with spirant mutation after a. An englyn is a short stanza of three or four lines, and Gwydion's three englynion are among the most obscure lines in the Four Branches; the English given here is tentative throughout. Dar a dyf 'an oak that grows' (dar 'oak', tyf 'grows', soft after a). deu lenn: deu 'two' causes soft mutation, so lenn may be glenn 'glen' or llenn 'covering'; which is meant is uncertain. Gorduwrych seems to be gor- 'very' + du 'dark' + a second element of uncertain meaning (brych 'speckled'?). Ony dywedaf i eu 'unless I speak falsely': eu is gau 'false', soft-mutated. O ulodeu Lleu ban yw hynn: blodeu 'flowers' soft after o; ban (pan) may be 'whence', giving 'this is from Lleu's flowers', perhaps a glance at Blodeuedd, who was made of flowers; the line is uncertain.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ynteu yr eryr, ymellwng yny oed yg kymerued y prenn.
sentences.l: That-is what did the eagle for-his-part, letting-himself-down until he-was in the middle of the tree.
sentences.i: And the eagle let himself down until he was in the middle of the tree.
sentences.n: ymellwng 'let oneself go, come down', ym- with ellwng (gollwng). It is written as one word with the second witness; Evans prints it once as ẏm ell6ng, in two pieces. yg kymerued 'in the middle' (yng nghymherfedd), the nasal mutation written g + k.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth ynteu Wydyon, canu englyn arall: “Dar a dyf yn ard uaes, Nis gwlych glaw, nis mwy tawd. Naw ugein angerd a borthes. Yn y blaen, Lleu Llaw Gyffes.”
sentences.l: That-is what did he-for-his-part Gwydion, singing another englyn: “An-oak that-grows in a-high plain, It-wets-it-not rain, it-melts-not more(?). Nine score onsets(?) it-has-borne. In its top, Lleu Llaw Gyffes.”
sentences.i: Then Gwydion sang another englyn: “An oak grows on a high plain; rain does not wet it, nor does it melt away. Nine score assaults it has borne. In its top, Lleu Llaw Gyffes.”
sentences.n: Ynteu Wydyon, soft after ynteu. yn ard uaes 'in a high plain': ard 'high' (cf. ardd 'height') with maes soft-mutated in the compound. Nis gwlych glaw 'rain does not wet it': nis is ny + s 'it'; gwlych is the 3rd singular present of gwlychu. nis mwy tawd is obscure: tawd looks like the 3rd singular present of toddi 'melt', mwy 'more', but the sense of the half-line is uncertain. The second witness reads 'mwy tawd nawes. Ugein angerd', which is not on the page; Evans, checked on the image, has nis m6ẏ ta6d. na6 ugein angerd, and the Red Book agrees. Naw ugein angerd a borthes 'nine score angerd it has borne': angerd is 'force, fury, passion' (angerdd), here perhaps storms or onslaughts; borthes is the 3rd singular preterite of porthi 'bear, endure'. Yn y blaen 'in its top'. Llaw Gyffes is the name given him earlier in the branch: llaw 'hand' (feminine) soft-mutates kyffes, usually taken as 'deft, sure'.

sentences.t: Ac yna ymellwng idaw ynteu, yny uyd yn y geing issaf o'r pren.
sentences.l: And then letting-himself-down by-him for-his-part, until he-is in the lowest branch of the tree.
sentences.i: And then he let himself down until he was on the lowest branch of the tree.
sentences.n: ymellwng idaw ynteu: idaw 'to him' here marks the eagle as the one who does it. yny uyd 'until he is': byd, the present of bot, soft after yny. y geing 'the branch': keing is feminine and soft-mutated after the article; it is the same word that names a 'branch' of the Mabinogi. issaf 'lowest'. pren is prenn, written with one n.

sentences.t: Canu englyn idaw ynteu yna: “Dar a dyf dan anwaeret, Mirein medur ymywet. Ony dywedaf i, ef dydau Lleu y'm arfet.”
sentences.l: Singing an-englyn to-him for-his-part then: “An-oak that-grows under a-slope, Fair [medur] [ymywet]. Unless I-speak, there-will-come Lleu into my lap.”
sentences.i: Then he sang an englyn to him: “An oak grows beneath a slope; fair … (the line is obscure). Unless I speak … Lleu will come into my lap.”
sentences.n: Canu englyn idaw 'singing an englyn to him', the eagle. dan anwaeret 'beneath a slope' (anwaered 'steep descent'). Mirein medur ymywet: mirein is 'fair, splendid' (mirain); the second witness reads modur, but Evans and the Red Book have medur, perhaps for modur 'ruler', though that is uncertain; ymywet is not explained with confidence. The line is left untranslated. Ony dywedaf i, ef dydau Lleu y'm arfet: dydau is the 3rd singular future of dyuot 'will come', and y'm arfet 'into my lap' is y 'into' + 'm 'my' + arffed. The White Book has no eu 'falsely' after dywedaf i, so the line falls short of the formula of the first englyn (Ony dywedaf i eu); the second witness adds [eu], the Red Book does not, and nothing is supplied. The English keeps the gap.

sentences.t: Ac y dygwydawd ynteu ar lin Gwydyon; ac yna y trewis Gwydyon a'r hutlath ynteu, yny uyd yn y rith e hunan.
sentences.l: And fell he-for-his-part on the knee of Gwydion; and then struck Gwydion with the magic-staff him, until he-is in his own form.
sentences.i: And he dropped on to Gwydion's knee; and then Gwydion struck him with the magic staff, so that he was in his own shape again.
sentences.n: dygwydawd is the 3rd singular preterite of dygwydaw 'fall', with the old ending -awd. ar lin: glin 'knee' soft-mutated after ar. trewis is the 3rd singular preterite of taraw 'strike'. hutlath 'magic staff', hut 'magic' + llath 'rod': Evans prints t, as the Red Book does, where the second witness has hudlath; kept, as in part 012. yn y rith e hunan 'in his own form'.

sentences.t: Ny welsei neb ar wr dremynt druanach hagen noc a oed arnaw ef.
sentences.l: Had-not-seen anyone on a-man an-aspect more-wretched, however, than was on-him.
sentences.i: No one had ever seen a more pitiful look on any man than there was on him.
sentences.n: welsei is gwelsei, the 3rd singular pluperfect of gwelet, soft after ny. ar wr 'on a man': gwr soft-mutated after ar. dremynt is tremynt 'look, aspect', soft-mutated as the object; druanach is truanach, comparative of truan 'wretched', soft-mutated after it. hagen 'however'. noc a oed arnaw ef 'than what was on him'.

sentences.t: Nit oed dim onyt croen ac ascwrn.
sentences.l: There-was-not anything but skin and bone.
sentences.i: There was nothing of him but skin and bone.
sentences.n: onyt 'but, except'. croen 'skin', ascwrn 'bone' (asgwrn).

sentences.t: Yna kyrchu Caer Dathyl a wnaeth ef, ac yno y ducpwyt a gahat o uedic da yg Gwyned wrthaw.
sentences.l: Then making-for Caer Dathyl he-did, and there was-brought what was-had of good physicians in Gwynedd to-him.
sentences.i: Then he made for Caer Dathyl, and there every good physician to be had in Gwynedd was brought to him.
sentences.n: The subject is Gwydion, bringing Lleu. ducpwyt is the impersonal preterite of dwyn 'bring'. a gahat 'what was had': cahat, impersonal preterite of cael, soft after a. o uedic: medic 'physician' soft-mutated after o. yg Gwyned 'in Gwynedd', the nasal written yg before G. wrthaw 'to him', to attend him.

sentences.t: Kyn kyuyl y'r ulwydyn, yd oed ef yn holl iach.
sentences.l: Before the end of the year, he-was wholly well.
sentences.i: Before the year was out, he was wholly healed.
sentences.n: kyuyl 'limit, end'. Evans prints ẏz (the r-rotunda), written y'r with the second witness (the Red Book has y2): 'to, of the year'. It may equally be read yr 'the', 'before the end of the year'; the sense is the same either way, and the reading is noted as in part 012's y'r dyd. y'r ulwydyn: blwydyn soft after the article. holl iach 'wholly well'.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb ef, wrth Math uab Mathonwy, “madws oed y mi caffael iawn gan y gwr y keueis ouut gantaw.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said he, to Math son of Mathonwy, “high-time it-were for-me getting redress from the man that I-got hurt from-him.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” he said to Math son of Mathonwy, “it is high time I had redress from the man who did me hurt.”
sentences.n: Lleu now speaks. madws 'high time, timely'. oed, the imperfect, again as 'it would be'. y mi 'for me'. iawn 'redress, compensation'. keueis is the 1st singular preterite of cael. ouut is gouut 'hurt, grief' (gofid), soft-mutated as the object. gantaw 'from him' picks up y gwr: 'the man I got hurt from him'.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb y Math, “ny eill ef ymgynhal, a'th iawn di gantaw.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said Math, “he-cannot hold-himself-up, and your redress with-him.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” said Math, “he cannot hold out while he still owes you redress.”
sentences.n: ny eill is the 3rd singular present of gallu. ymgynhal 'hold oneself up, hold out' (ymgynnal). a'th iawn di gantaw 'and your redress with him': an absolute phrase, 'with your due still in his keeping'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “goreu yw genhyf i bo kyntaf y caffwyf iawn.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “best is with-me that soonest I-may-get redress.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “the sooner I have redress, the better I shall like it.”
sentences.n: goreu yw genhyf 'best it is with me', I like best. genhyf 'with me' (gennyf). bo 'that it be', present subjunctive of bot. kyntaf 'soonest'. caffwyf 'I may get'.

sentences.t: Yna dygyuoryaw Gwyned a wnaethant, a chyrchu Ardudwy.
sentences.l: Then mustering Gwynedd they-did, and making-for Ardudwy.
sentences.i: Then they mustered Gwynedd and made for Ardudwy.
sentences.n: dygyuoryaw 'muster, raise (a host)' (dygyfor), closed by a wnaethant.

sentences.t: Gwydyon a gerdwys yn y blaen, a chyrchu Mur Castell a oruc.
sentences.l: Gwydion it-was-that went in the van, and making-for Mur Castell he-did.
sentences.i: Gwydion went on ahead and made for Mur Castell.
sentences.n: yn y blaen 'in the front'. a chyrchu … a oruc: kyrchu with spirant mutation after a, closed by a oruc. Mur Castell is Lleu's court in Ardudwy, where Blodeuedd is.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth Blodeuwed, clybot eu bot yn dyuot, kymryt y morynyon gyt a hi, a chyrchu y mynyd; a thrwy Auon Gynuael kyrchu llys a oed ar y mynyd.
sentences.l: That-is what did Blodeuedd, hearing their being coming, taking the maidens with her, and making-for the mountain; and across the River Cynfael making-for a-court that was on the mountain.
sentences.i: When Blodeuedd heard that they were coming, she took her maidens with her and made for the mountain; and across the river Cynfael she made for a court that stood on the mountain.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth Blodeuwed: the sef pattern with three verbal nouns. The name is written Blodeuwed from here on, Blodeued earlier; the English keeps Blodeuedd. clybot 'hear' (clywed). eu bot yn dyuot 'their being coming', that they were coming. morynyon 'maidens' (morwynion). gyt a hi 'with her'. a thrwy: trwy 'through, across' with spirant mutation after a.

sentences.t: Ac ni wydyn gerdet rac ouyn, namyn ac eu hwyneb tra eu keuyn.
sentences.l: And they-knew-not walking for fear, but with their face behind their back.
sentences.i: And for fear they could not walk except with their faces turned back over their shoulders.
sentences.n: ni wydyn 'they did not know (how)': gwydyn, 3rd plural imperfect of gwybot, soft after ni. rac ouyn 'for fear': ofn soft after rac. namyn 'except'. ac eu hwyneb 'with their face': ac is a 'with' before a vowel, and eu puts h before wyneb. tra eu keuyn 'beyond their back', looking behind them.

sentences.t: Ac yna ni wybuant yny syrthyssant yn y llyn ac y bodyssant oll eithyr hi e hunan.
sentences.l: And then they-knew-not until they-fell into the lake and were-drowned all except her herself.
sentences.i: And then, before they knew it, they had fallen into the lake and were all drowned but she alone.
sentences.n: wybuant is gwybuant, 3rd plural preterite of gwybot, soft after ni. syrthyssant 'they fell' and bodyssant 'they drowned' (bodi) have the 3rd plural preterite ending -yssant. The text does not name the lake; tradition gives the name Llyn y Morwynion, 'the maidens' lake', to a lake in Ardudwy. eithyr 'except'; hi e hunan 'she herself'.

sentences.t: Ac yna y gordiwawd Gwydyon hitheu, ac y dywot wrthi, “Ny ladaf i di.
sentences.l: And then overtook Gwydion her-for-her-part, and said to-her, “I-will-not-kill you.
sentences.i: And then Gwydion overtook her, and said to her, “I will not kill you.
sentences.n: gordiwawd is the 3rd singular preterite of goddiwes 'overtake', with the -awd ending. ny ladaf: lladaf soft-mutated after ny.

sentences.t: Mi a wnaf yssyd waeth it. Sef yw hynny,” heb ef, “dy ellwng yn rith ederyn.
sentences.l: I it-is-that will-do what-is worse to-you. That-is is that,” said he, “letting-you-go in the-form of a-bird.
sentences.i: I will do what is worse for you. That is,” he said, “to let you go in the form of a bird.
sentences.n: yssyd waeth 'what is worse': gwaeth soft-mutated after yssyd. it 'to you'. dy ellwng 'your letting go': gellwng soft after dy. ederyn 'bird' (aderyn).

sentences.t: Ac o achaws y kywilyd a wnaethost ti y Lew Llaw Gyffes, na ueidych ditheu dangos dy wyneb lliw dyd byth, a hynny rac ouyn yr holl adar.
sentences.l: And because of the shame that you-did to Lleu Llaw Gyffes, that you-dare-not show your face by-light of-day ever, and that for fear of all the birds.
sentences.i: And because of the shame you did to Lleu Llaw Gyffes, you shall never dare show your face by daylight, and that for fear of all the birds.
sentences.n: kywilyd 'shame' (cywilydd). wnaethost is the 2nd singular preterite of gwneuthur. y Lew 'to Lleu': the narrative spells the name Llew (soft-mutated here after y 'to'), as it does to the end of the branch, where the englynion wrote Lleu; the English keeps Lleu. na ueidych 'that you may not dare': na with beidych, 2nd singular present subjunctive of beidyaw 'dare', soft-mutated; the subjunctive gives the sentence the force of a doom. lliw dyd 'colour of day', daylight. rac ouyn 'for fear of'.

sentences.t: A bot gelynyaeth y rynghot a'r holl adar. A bot yn anyan udunt dy uaedu; a'th amherchi, y lle i'th gaffant. Ac na chollych dy enw, namyn dy alw uyth yn Blodeuwed.”
sentences.l: And being enmity between-you and all the birds. And being in nature to-them your beating; and your dishonouring, the place that they-find-you. And that you-lose-not your name, but your calling ever Blodeuedd.”
sentences.i: And there shall be enmity between you and all the birds, and it shall be their nature to strike you and to ill-use you wherever they find you. And you shall not lose your name, but shall be called for ever Blodeuedd.”
sentences.n: The doom goes on in verbal nouns: A bot 'and (there shall) be'. gelynyaeth 'enmity'. y rynghot 'between you' (rhyngot). anyan 'nature' (anian); udunt 'to them'. dy uaedu 'your beating': baedu soft after dy. amherchi 'dishonour, ill-treat' (amharchu). y lle i'th gaffant 'the place they find you': i is the particle y, 'th the infixed 'you', and caffant the 3rd plural present subjunctive of cael. na chollych: collych, 2nd singular present subjunctive of colli 'lose', with spirant mutation after na. yn Blodeuwed 'as Blodeuedd': the name is not mutated after yn. The form Blodeuwed, with -wed, looks like gwedd 'face, aspect', 'flower-face', an apt name for an owl; the English keeps the one form, Blodeuedd.

sentences.t: Sef yw Blodeuwed, tylluan o'r ieith yr awr honn.
sentences.l: That-is is Blodeuedd, owl in the language of this-time.
sentences.i: Blodeuedd is the word for 'owl' in the speech of the present day.
sentences.n: Sef yw 'that is', here explaining a word: Blodeuwed is 'owl' (tylluan) in the language of the teller's own day. yr awr honn 'this time, now'.

sentences.t: Ac o achaws hynny y mae digassawc yr adar y'r tylluan.
sentences.l: And because of that is hostile the birds to the owl.
sentences.i: And for that reason the birds are hostile to the owl.
sentences.n: y mae 'is' with its predicate digassawc 'hostile, full of hatred' (digasog) before the subject yr adar 'the birds'. y'r tylluan 'to the owl': here tylluan is left unmutated after the article, though it is feminine; the next sentence has y dylluan.

sentences.t: Ac ef a elwir etwa y dylluan yn Blodeuwed.
sentences.l: And it it-is-that is-called still the owl Blodeuedd.
sentences.i: And the owl is still called Blodeuedd.
sentences.n: ef a elwir 'it is called': empty ef and gelwir, impersonal present of galw, soft after a. etwa 'still' (eto). y dylluan: tylluan soft-mutated after the article, as a feminine noun should be.

sentences.t: Ynteu Gronwy Pebyr a gyrchwys Penllyn, ac odyno yngynnatau a wnaeth.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Gronw Pebyr it-was-that made-for Penllyn, and from-there sending-envoys he-did.
sentences.i: Gronw Pebyr made for Penllyn, and from there he sent envoys.
sentences.n: The name is written Gronwy here and in most of what follows, Gronw earlier; the English keeps Gronw (but Llech Gronwy below is a place-name and keeps its form). gyrchwys is kyrchwys, 3rd singular preterite of kyrchu, soft after a. odyno 'from there' (oddi yno). yngynnatau 'send envoys, send messages': Evans prints yngynnatau with n (zoom 12), where the second witness has ymgynnatau and the Red Book ymgennattau. It is kept as written: the reflexive ym- written yn- before g, with kennat 'messenger'.

sentences.t: Sef kennadwri a anuones, gouyn a wnaeth y Lew Llaw Gyffes, a uynnei ae tir ae dayar, ae eur, ae aryant, am y sarhaet.
sentences.l: That-is the message that he-sent, asking he-did of Lleu Llaw Gyffes, whether he-wanted either land or ground, or gold, or silver, for his insult.
sentences.i: The message he sent was to ask Lleu Llaw Gyffes whether he would have land or ground, or gold, or silver, for the insult done him.
sentences.n: Sef kennadwri a anuones 'that is the message he sent': sef again pointing ahead. kennadwri 'message, embassy'. gouyn a wnaeth y 'he asked of'. y Lew: Llew soft after y. a uynnei 'whether he would want': mynnei, imperfect of mynnu, soft after a. ae … ae 'either … or' (ai … ai). tir 'land', dayar 'ground, earth'. sarhaet is the insult and also the fine due in law for it (sarhaed).

sentences.t: “Na chymeraf, y Duw dygaf uyg kyffes,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “I-will-not-take, to God I-bear my confession,” said he.
sentences.i: “I will not take it, as I make my confession to God,” he said.
sentences.n: Na chymeraf 'I will not take': na, the negative of a reply, with spirant mutation, kymeraf > chymeraf. y Duw dygaf uyg kyffes 'to God I bear my confession', an oath. uyg kyffes is fy nghyffes, the nasal written g + k.

sentences.t: “A llyma y peth lleiaf a gymeraf y gantaw; mynet y'r lle yd oedwn i ohonaw ef, ban i'm byryawd a'r par, a minheu y lle yd oed ynteu.
sentences.l: “And here-is the least thing that I-will-take from-him: going by-him to the place I-was, when he-struck-me with the spear, and me in the place he-was.
sentences.i: “And this is the least I will take from him: that he go to the place where I was when he struck me with the spear, and I be in the place where he was.
