sentences.n: llyma 'here is'. lleiaf 'least'. y gantaw 'from him'. mynet … ohonaw ef 'going by him', that he should go. yd oedwn i 'I was' (1st singular imperfect of bot). ban i'm byryawd 'when he struck me': ban is pan, i'm is the particle y with the infixed 'm 'me' (Evans writes im; the Red Book pan ym), and byryawd the 3rd singular preterite of bwrw with the -awd ending. par 'spear'. minheu 'I in my turn'.

sentences.t: A gadel y minheu y uwrw ef a phar. A hynny leiaf peth a gymeraf y gantaw.”
sentences.l: And letting to-me myself casting-at him with a-spear. And that, least thing that I-will-take from-him.
sentences.i: And that I be let cast at him with a spear. That is the least I will take from him.”
sentences.n: gadel 'let, leave'. y minheu 'to me myself'. y uwrw ef 'to cast at him': bwrw soft after y. a phar 'with a spear': par with spirant mutation after a. A hynny leiaf peth 'and that (is the) least thing': lleiaf soft-mutated.

sentences.t: Hynny a uenegit y Gronw Bebyr.
sentences.l: That it-was-that was-told to Gronw Pebyr.
sentences.i: This was told to Gronw Pebyr.
sentences.n: uenegit is menegit, the impersonal imperfect of menegi 'tell', soft after a. y Gronw 'to Gronw': the name is not mutated after y. The epithet is written Bebyr here and in the sentences that follow, Pebyr elsewhere: the soft mutation an epithet often takes after a personal name; the English keeps Pebyr.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “dir yw ymi gwneuthur hynny. Wy gwyrda kywir, a'm teulu, a'm brodyr maeth, a oes ohonawch chwi, a gymero yr ergyt drossof i?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “necessary is to-me doing that. O noblemen true, and my household-troop, and my foster-brothers, is-there of-you who-will-take the cast for-me?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “I must needs do it. My true noblemen, and my warband, and my foster-brothers: is there any one of you who will take the cast in my stead?”
sentences.n: dir 'needful, certain': dir yw ymi 'it is needful for me'. Wy is an exclamation, 'O', before the persons addressed. gwyrda 'noblemen'; kywir 'true, loyal'. a'm teulu 'and my warband' (the household-troop). brodyr maeth 'foster-brothers'. a oes 'is there'. ohonawch chwi 'of you' (o, 2nd plural). a gymero 'who will take': kymero, 3rd singular present subjunctive of kymryt, soft after a. ergyt 'cast'. drossof 'for me, in my place' (dros, 1st singular).

sentences.t: “Nac oes, dioer,” heb wynt.
sentences.l: “There-is-not, assuredly,” said they.
sentences.i: “No, indeed,” they said.
sentences.n: Nac oes 'there is not': the reply repeats the verb of the question, oes, with the negative nac. heb wynt 'said they'.

sentences.t: Ac o achaws gomed ohonunt wy diodef kymryt un ergyt dros eu harglwyd, y gelwir wynteu, yr hynny hyt hediw, trydyd anniweir deulu.
sentences.l: And because of refusing by-them to-suffer taking one cast for their lord, they-are-called, they-for-their-part, from that until today, the third faithless warband.
sentences.i: And because they refused to bear the taking of one cast for their lord, they are called, from that day to this, one of the Three Faithless Warbands.
sentences.n: gomed 'refuse' (gomedd); ohonunt wy 'by them'. diodef 'suffer, endure'. dros eu harglwyd 'for their lord': eu puts h before arglwyd. y gelwir 'they are called': gelwir, impersonal present of galw. yr hynny hyt hediw 'from then until today'. trydyd anniweir deulu 'the third faithless warband' is the language of the Triads, where a set of three is named and each member is 'the third': this warband is one of the Three Faithless Warbands of the Island of Britain. anniweir 'unfaithful' stands before its noun and soft-mutates it, teulu > deulu.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ef, “mi a'e kymeraf.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he, “I it-is-that will-take-it.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “I will take it.”
sentences.n: mi a'e kymeraf: the infixed 'e 'it' between a and the verb, as in mi a'e dywedaf earlier.

sentences.t: Ac yna y doethant yll deu hyt ar lan Auon Gynuael.
sentences.l: And then came they the two-of-them as-far-as to the bank of the River Cynfael.
sentences.i: And then the two of them came to the bank of the river Cynfael.
sentences.n: yll deu 'the two of them' (ill dau). hyt ar 'as far as on to'. ar lan: glan soft after ar.

sentences.t: Ac yna y seui Gronwy Bebyr, yn y lle yd oed Llew Llaw Gyffes ban y byryawd ef, a Llew yn y lle yd oed ynteu.
sentences.l: And then stood Gronw Pebyr, in the place was Lleu Llaw Gyffes when he-struck him, and Lleu in the place was he.
sentences.i: And then Gronw Pebyr stood where Lleu Llaw Gyffes had stood when he struck him, and Lleu where Gronw had been.
sentences.n: seui is the 3rd singular imperfect of sefyll 'stand'. Evans prints yseuit with the t dotted beneath, the scribe's mark of deletion, and the t is left out (the Red Book has yseuif). ban y byryawd ef 'when he struck him': ef here is Lleu, the object.

sentences.t: Ac yna y dyuot Gronwy Bebyr wrth Llew, “Arglwyd,” heb ef, “canys o drycystryw gwreic y gwneuthum yti a wneuthum, minheu a archaf yti, yr Duw, llech a welaf ar lan yr auon, gadel ym dodi honno y rynghof a'r dyrnawt.”
sentences.l: And then said Gronw Pebyr to Lleu, “Lord,” said he, “since it-is by the evil-contriving of a-woman that I-did to-you what I-did, I-for-my-part ask of-you, for God, a-stone that I-see on the bank of the river, letting me put that between-me and the blow.”
sentences.i: And then Gronw Pebyr said to Lleu, “Lord, since it was through a woman's wicked contriving that I did to you what I did, I ask you, for God's sake, to let me put the stone I see on the river bank between me and the blow.”
sentences.n: y dyuot 'said': in this sense the word must be dywot, the preterite of dywedut, though the spelling is that of dyuot 'come'. o drycystryw gwreic 'through a woman's evil contrivance': drycystryw (drwg + ystryw) soft-mutated after o. y gwneuthum yti a wneuthum 'that I did to you what I did': the cause is put first and y introduces the rest. archaf 'I ask' (erchi). llech 'slab, flat stone' stands first and is picked up by honno 'that one'. gadel ym dodi 'letting me put'. y rynghof 'between me' (rhyngof). dyrnawt 'blow'.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb y Llew, “ni'th omedaf o hynny.”
sentences.l: “Assuredly,” said Lleu, “I-will-not-refuse-you of that.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” said Lleu, “I will not refuse you that.”
sentences.n: ni'th omedaf 'I will not refuse you': the infixed 'th soft-mutates gomedaf, 1st singular present of gomed 'refuse'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ef, “Duw a dalho it.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he, “God may-he-repay to-you.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “may God repay you.”
sentences.n: Duw a dalho it, the formula of thanks.

sentences.t: Ac yna y kymerth Gronwy y llech ac y dodes y ryngtaw a'r ergyt.
sentences.l: And then took Gronw the stone and set it between-him and the cast.
sentences.i: And then Gronw took the stone and set it between himself and the cast.
sentences.n: kymerth 'took', dodes 'set'. y ryngtaw 'between him' (rhyngddo).

sentences.t: Ac yna y byryawd Llew ef a'r par, ac y guant y llech drwydi, ac ynteu drwydaw, yny dyrr y geuynn.
sentences.l: And then struck Lleu him with the spear, and pierced the stone through-it, and him through-him, until breaks his back.
sentences.i: And then Lleu cast the spear at him, and it went right through the stone and through him, so that his back was broken.
sentences.n: byryawd 'struck, cast' (bwrw). guant is the 3rd singular preterite of gwanu 'pierce, thrust'. drwydi 'through it' (trwy, 3rd singular feminine, for the llech); drwydaw 'through him'. yny dyrr 'so that breaks': tyrr, the 3rd singular present of torri, soft after yny. y geuynn 'his back': keuyn soft after y 'his'.

sentences.t: Ac yna y llas Gronwy Bebyr, ac yno y mae y llech ar lan Auon Gynuael yn Ardudwy, a'r twll drwydi.
sentences.l: And then was-killed Gronw Pebyr, and there is the stone on the bank of the River Cynfael in Ardudwy, and the hole through-it.
sentences.i: And so Gronw Pebyr was slain; and there the stone lies, on the bank of the river Cynfael in Ardudwy, with the hole through it.
sentences.n: llas is the impersonal preterite of llad 'kill', 'was killed'. yno y mae 'there is'. twll 'hole'; drwydi 'through it'.

sentences.t: Ac o achaws hynny ettwa y gelwir Llech Gronwy.
sentences.l: And because of that still it-is-called Llech Gronwy.
sentences.i: And that is why it is still called Llech Gronwy.
sentences.n: ettwa is etwa 'still'. y gelwir 'it is called'. Llech Gronwy, 'Gronw's stone', keeps the form of the name the text gives.

sentences.t: Ynteu Llew Llaw Gyffes a oreskynnwys eilweith y wlat, ac a'y gwledychwys yn llwydanhus.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Lleu Llaw Gyffes it-was-that conquered a-second-time the land, and that ruled-it prosperously.
sentences.i: Lleu Llaw Gyffes took possession of the land a second time, and ruled it prosperously.
sentences.n: oreskynnwys is goreskynnwys, 3rd singular preterite of goresgyn, soft after a. eilweith 'a second time'. ac a'y gwledychwys 'and ruled it': Evans prints a small a above the line after ac (zoom 14), brought into the line here, where the second witness reads ac y. a'y is the relative a with the infixed y 'it', feminine, for gwlat, and gwledychwys is unmutated after it. llwydanhus 'prosperously' (llwyddiannus).

sentences.t: A herwyd y dyweit y kyuarwydyt, ef a uu arglwyd wedy hynny ar Wyned.
sentences.l: And according-as says the story, he it-was-that was lord after that over Gwynedd.
sentences.i: And as the story tells, he was afterwards lord over Gwynedd.
sentences.n: herwyd 'according as'. dyweit is the 3rd singular present of dywedut. kyuarwydyt is the storyteller's lore, the tale as tradition has it (cyfarwyddyd). ar Wyned: Gwyned soft-mutated after ar.

sentences.t: Ac yuelly y teruyna y geing honn o'r Mabinogi.
sentences.l: And thus ends this branch of the Mabinogi.
sentences.i: And so ends this branch of the Mabinogi.
sentences.n: The closing formula, in col. 111 l. 16. It ends the Fourth Branch, and with it the Four Branches: col. 111 is a short column, and col. 112 is empty. yuelly 'thus' (felly). teruyna is the 3rd singular present of teruynu 'end'. y geing honn 'this branch': keing soft after the article. The meaning and origin of the word Mabinogi are disputed.
